newsitem.title: USA: Arizona voters back lottery measure -- officials.
newsitem.headline: Arizona voters back lottery measure -- officials.

text.p: An Arizona initiative that would allocate $17 million annually to fund health and nutrition programs appeared to pass on Tuesday, according to election returns.
Proposition 203, which would allocate the funds from lottery revenues, had 71.1 percent support, while 28.8 percent were opposed, with nearly 70 percent of precincts reporting.
Proposition 201, which would amend gambling agreements between the state and Indian tribes, was winning approval by 63.2 percent to 36.7 percent, election officials said.

The vote on Proposition 101, which would allow the legislature to exempt from taxation the first $50,000 of the value of personal property that is used for agricultural purposes or in a trade or business, was too close to call, with the "yes" vote narrowly ahead.
